name: What is the difference between a site visit and a feasibility study?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a construction site visit and a full feasibility study?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a construction site visit and a full feasibility study?

acceptedAnswer.text: A site visit is usually the first-step inspection: it focuses on what can be seen on the ground, such as access, slope, existing improvements, drainage patterns, and obvious constraints. A feasibility study is broader and more decision-focused. It combines site observations with zoning review, permitting checks, utility availability, rough cost estimating, and risk analysis to answer whether the project should move forward at all. For owners evaluating a Los Angeles property, the feasibility study is much more useful when the site has complexity, such as a hillside lot, narrow frontage, or a teardown with unknown constraints. If the goal is to make a purchase or green-light design, a feasibility study usually provides the stronger decision-making document.
acceptedAnswer.description: A site visit is a quick on-site review of visible conditions, while a feasibility study is a deeper analysis of whether the project can be built, permitted, and budgeted realistically. A feasibility study usually adds zoning review, utility checks, risk analysis, cost ranges, and schedule implications.
